walkthroughs.body_html:
Nature & Variety of Living Organisms — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Nature & Variety of Living Organisms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Nature & Variety of Living Organisms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a prokaryote?
options: Human skin cell
Yeast
Bacterium
Onion cell
protein synthesis
photosynthesis
aerobic respiration
cell division

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.

mcqs.q: Why are X-linked recessive conditions more common in males?
options: X-linked conditions affect only males because females cannot inherit X-linked alleles.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
X-linked recessive conditions affect more males because the Y chromosome makes the disease worse.
Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is expressed — there's no second X to mask it.

mcqs.q: What does insulin do to blood glucose?
options: It lowers blood glucose by causing cells (especially liver and muscle) to take it up and store it as glycogen.
Insulin raises blood glucose to give the body energy.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Prokaryotic cell”?
options: A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Specialised cells”?
options: Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Eukaryotic cell”?
options: The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Subcellular structures”?
options: Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cell”?
options: Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Stem cell”?
options: Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
